name: Lacunal Collector
body:
LACUNAL COLLECTOR
CR 11

XP 12,800
LE Medium undead (android)
Init +8; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +31

DEFENSE

AC 25, touch 15, flat-footed 20 (+4 Dex, +1 dodge, +10 natural)
hp 136 (16d8+64); regeneration 10 (see text)
Fort +9, Ref +11, Will +16
Defensive Abilities channel resistance +4, spontaneous reincarnation; Immune undead traits; Weakness collection dependency

OFFENSE

Speed 50 ft.
Melee +1 sentinel spear +16/+11/+6 (1d8+5/×3 P)
Ranged zero rifle +16/+11/+6 touch (2d6 cold, range incr. 150 ft., automatic)
Special Attacks memory extraction (DC 22)
Spells Known (CL 11th, concentration +15, +19 to cast defensively)

0-level (at will)—detect magic, grave words, mage hand, prestidigitation, read magic, telekinetic projectile
1st-level (6/day)—bane (DC 16), earpiercing scream (DC 15), detect good, inflict light wounds, lesser confusion (DC 16), protection from good
2nd-level (5/day)—daze monster (DC 17), fog cloud, hold person (DC 17), inflict pain (DC 17), reject augmentation (DC 16; see page 25)
3rd-level (5/day)—chain of perdition, deep slumber (DC 18), phantasmal asphyxiation HA (DC 17), synaptic pulse (DC 18)
4th-level (3/day)—fear (DC 18), inflict critical wounds (DC 18), mind thrust IV (DC 18)

STATISTICS

Str 16 (+3); Dex 18 (+4); Con —; Int 20 (+5); Wis 23 (+6); Cha 18 (+4)
Base Atk +12; CMB +15; CMD 30
Feats Combat Casting, Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Improved Initiative, Lightning Reflexes, Skill Focus (Perception), Spell Focus (enchantment), Technologist
Skills Disable Device +20, Intimidate +23, Knowledge (arcana, religion) +24, Knowledge (engineering) +21, Perception +31, Sense Motive +23, Spellcraft +24, Stealth +23
Languages Common
SQ augmented scavenger, constructed, flat affect

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Augmented Scavenger (Ex)

See above.

Collection Dependency (Su)

Each time a lacunal collector transfers their consciousness into a new body, their previous head sloughs off and is replaced by a new one. Lacunal collectors keep their decaying heads and often wear them as ornamentation. A lacunal collector typically has 1d6+1 additional heads. A creature can target one of these grisly trophies with a melee or ranged attack; add +2 to the lacunal collector’s AC if attempting this attack. If the attack hits, that head is automatically destroyed. Destroying all of a lacunal collector’s heads ends the creature’s regeneration ability.

Constructed (Ex)

See above.

Flat Affect (Ex)

See above.

Memory Extraction (Su)

See above.

Spellcasting See above.

Spontaneous Reincarnation (Su)

See above.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary, pair, or enclave (1–2 plus 4–6 lacunal initiates)
Treasure standard (+1 sentinel spear, zero rifle, 2 silverdisk batteries [10 charges each], other treasure)

While androids do not age, and could theoretically live forever, it is a fact of the universe that things fall apart—as time marches on, everything gradually moves to a state of greater entropy. Androids sense this progression of time, and realize that like other beings their place in the universe is fleeting. Usually around 100 years of age—sometimes more, sometimes less—they feel a sense of accomplishment and are ready to “reset,” allowing their mind and soul to pass into the afterlife, while their body is recycled or refurbished to serve as the shell for a new android life.

However, for some androids, just as for some members of other humanoid species, the temptation of eternal life becomes too great, and they push their physical bodies to their limits—and beyond. The obscure Cult of Lacuna is devoted to giving these androids what they seek, using occult rituals to transform them into undead creatures.

When an android first joins the Cult of Lacuna, it constructs a new techno-organic body for itself, and its consciousness is transferred into this new undead receptacle.

Its old body withers and dies, and the initiate saves the head as a trophy.

Periodically, a lacunal android must complete this ritual again, and each time, it saves the old head for its collection. It wears these heads like trophies, often wired to its body like grim animatronic novelties.
